description: Weekly. pytest-homeassistant-custom-component follows Home Assistant's own release cadence and publishes several times a week, so a daily run raises the same upgrade repeatedly before anyone has looked at the first one.

Nothing automerges. The suite does exercise the real Sonos and apple_tv modules, so a green run is genuine evidence for ruff and for the actions — but it is the same suite either side of a Home Assistant bump, and what that bump changes is the seam being tested, which is exactly what a passing run cannot speak to.

packageRules.description: These are not this project's dependencies. requirements_test.txt pins them to whatever Home Assistant pins, because importing homeassistant.components.sonos pulls the whole chain and the DIDL assertions are only meaningful against the soco a speaker actually receives bytes from. Taking the newest release from PyPI would test a stack no install has: the tests would keep passing while proving less. They move when the Home Assistant pin below moves, by reading what that release pins, which is not a thing Renovate can see.

This one pin is the Home Assistant upgrade: the package pulls Home Assistant in, so its version decides which core the grafts are patched onto and which apple_tv module the seams are read from. It gets its own pull request, never grouped, because the diff is one line and the review is the release notes of a different project.

ruff is pinned so that `ruff check` means the same thing run to run; its default rule set moves between releases. An upgrade that fails CI is a rule set that changed, which is the thing worth knowing.
